newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan halts reactor after leakage news delay-media.
newsitem.headline: Japan halts reactor after leakage news delay-media.

text.p: The state-run firm accused of covering up its mishandling of Japan's worst nuclear accident last month was ordered by authorities to shut down a separate atomic reactor late on Tuesday after another mishap, Japanese media reported on Wednesday.

Japanese authorities on Tuesday ordered the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) to halt operations at an advanced thermal reactor in western Japan after it learned the state-run body had delayed reporting a radiation leak, Kyodo news agency said.

The PNC, already facing possible legal action over its handling of an accident last month at a nuclear fuel reprocessing plant northeast of Tokyo, waited 30 hours before reporting a leakage at its "Fugen" advanced thermal reactor in Tsuruga, Fukui Prefecture, Kyodo quoted authorities as saying.

Fukui prefectural government officials said an alarm went off early on Monday after a high level of the radioactive material tritium was detected in a facility at the Fugen reactor, Japan's only heavy water reactor, the Kyodo report said. Other Japanese media carried similar reports.
PNC officials found that heavy water had leaked from a pipe in the facility, but did not report the accident to local or national authorities until Tuesday, 30 hours after the tritium leakage.
"Our report was delayed because of our misjudgment. I am sorry for causing trouble," Norito Takeshita, head of the Fugen nuclear plant, was quoted by Kyodo as telling a news conference on Tuesday.

In a separate development on Tuesday, officials from the Science and Technology Agency, which overseas Japan's ambitious nuclear power programme, said they would file a complaint with prosecutors or police against the PNC as early as Wednesday over the earlier accident.

The complaint, which would initiate legal action against the state-run firm or its officials, concerns inaccuracies in a PNC report on a March 11 fire and explosion at a nuclear reprocessing plant which exposed 37 workers to low levels of radiation.

The PNC admitted last week that the report was deliberately altered to suggest, falsely, that plant workers had checked to ensure that the fire had been doused. The fire flared up later, triggering the explosion.

In an earlier case of PNC deception, PNC officials in December 1995 admitted they had lied about inspections and tried to suppress videotape footage of a massive coolant leak at the firm's experimental fast-breeder reactor, Monju, which is located near the site of Monday's leakage.
